investigation_type: Discovery; native reconstruction; cross-workflow execution continuity test; universal objective-level causal graph test

presentation.investigation_summary:
Source status: REFINE — CROSS-WORKFLOW EXECUTION CONTINUITY EXISTS NATIVELY; A DISTINCT ART GAP IS NOT YET DEMONSTRATED

ServiceNow has strong native cross-workflow execution continuity. The platform supports modular workflows, parent/child execution linkage, persistent waiting states, cross-context timelines, agentic execution history, episodic memory, human supervision, and cross-system execution. The broad "execution intelligence" capability gap is rejected. The only remaining hypothesis is whether ServiceNow lacks a unified objective-level causal execution graph connecting the complete chain from business objective to final outcome.

1. A real ServiceNow exception workflow (Intelligent Approvals) was identified where automation reaches an exception, prompting a human into the loop.
2. The initial broad hypothesis was that ART can provide execution intelligence beyond ServiceNow.
3. Over successive checkpoints, the evidence confirmed that ServiceNow already has sophisticated exception handling, human approvals, supervised AI, escalation workflows, contextual AI interaction, and auditability.
4. The investigation focused on cross-workflow continuity. ServiceNow's Workflow Studio, subflows, timelines, and agentic workflows were tested.
5. The broad ART proposition was falsified by evidence of native cross-workflow continuity, persistent state, and agent memory.
6. **Final:** The hypothesis narrowed to "Objective-level causal execution continuity across heterogeneous workflows, agents, systems and human decisions." Whether ServiceNow natively provides this is currently unknown. **REFINE.**

key_findings.statement: ServiceNow Intelligent Approvals fallback to human — Exception workflow verified; AI "can't decide" state verified.
Subflows, parent/child execution visibility — Native cross-workflow continuity established.
Waiting state and persistent workflow context — Native ability to persist interrupted workflow state established.
Workflow timelines across multiple contexts — Ability to reconstruct relationships between workflow execution contexts established.
Agentic execution history and episodic memory — Native agent execution memory established.
Universal objective-level causal graph — Residual hypothesis survives for further testing.

decision.decision: **REFINE OPP-009.** Do not proceed with the generic "execution intelligence" opportunity. Retain the working opportunity as a narrowly defined research question on objective-level causal execution graphs. Do not create AIL intake. Proceed to the next checkpoint (OPP-009-08).
decision.reason:
ServiceNow has strong native cross-workflow execution continuity. The platform supports modular workflows, parent/child execution linkage, persistent waiting states, cross-context timelines, agentic execution history, episodic memory, human supervision, and cross-system execution. The broad "execution intelligence" capability gap is rejected. The only remaining hypothesis is whether ServiceNow lacks a unified objective-level causal execution graph connecting the complete chain from business objective to final outcome.

This representation gives ServiceNow its strongest reasonable native interpretation. It establishes that cross-workflow execution continuity is not missing. The only unresolved question is whether a unified objective-level causal execution model exists natively. No capability gap is declared. No commercial value is inferred.

primary_question:
Whether ServiceNow can natively preserve causal execution context across multiple workflows, agents, systems, and human decisions belonging to one business objective

The initial question was whether a real ServiceNow workflow could be identified in which normal agentic automation reaches an exception and brings a human into the loop, creating a live execution situation where ART could potentially add measurable value. The broad hypothesis was that ART can provide execution intelligence beyond ServiceNow's native capabilities.

evidence.statement: ServiceNow Intelligent Approvals fallback to human
Subflows, parent/child execution visibility
Waiting state and persistent workflow context
Workflow timelines across multiple contexts
Agentic execution history and episodic memory
Universal objective-level causal graph

ServiceNow documents **Intelligent Approvals** as an AI-driven approval workflow.
Its decision path is:
APPROVAL REQUEST
↓
AI EVALUATION
↓
┌──────────────┬──────────────┐
↓              ↓              ↓
AUTO-APPROVE  AUTO-REJECT   CAN'T DECIDE
↓
HUMAN APPROVAL
ServiceNow states that when AI cannot confidently determine the outcome, the request falls back to the existing approval workflow and is routed to a human approval user.
Source:
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/build-workflows/explore-intelligent-approvals.html

The workflow contains the required transition:
AUTOMATED DECISION
↓
AMBIGUITY
↓
HUMAN PARTICIPATION
↓
DECISION
↓
WORKFLOW CONTINUES
ServiceNow documents that routine requests can be automatically approved or rejected, while ambiguous requests are routed to human approvers. Human reviewers receive work notes indicating that AI attempted evaluation but could not determine an outcome, and approval decisions remain recorded.
Source:
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/build-workflows/explore-intelligent-approvals.html

WORKFLOW CONTINUES
Source:
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/build-workflows/explore-intelligent-approvals.html

ServiceNow does not send the human into a context-free approval state. Human approval users receive work notes indicating that AI attempted evaluation but could not determine an outcome.
Source:
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/build-workflows/explore-intelligent-approvals.html

ServiceNow also provides an **Identify escalation signals** agentic workflow. It evaluates active tickets using factors including priority, urgency, impact, ticket age, reassignment count, sentiment trends, SLA proximity and similar-record history.
